sources.title: Artificial Intelligence in Chrome
sources.inspected: Built-in AI overview and API navigation.
sources.use: Selected currently documented browser capabilities rather than promising universal support.

sources.title: The Prompt API
sources.inspected: Availability/create/prompt/destroy, expectedInputs/expectedOutputs, supported languages and audio modality.
sources.use: Optional English reflection coach. Urdu is not in the listed supported languages; no Urdu pronunciation assessment is claimed.

sources.title: SpeechSynthesis: getVoices()
sources.inspected: Device voice enumeration and voiceschanged example.
sources.use: Runtime Urdu/Hindi voice detection and an explicit unsupported state.

sources.title: SpeechRecognition: processLocally
sources.inspected: Local recognition property and language-pack requirement.
sources.use: Local-only recognition request; no remote fallback.

sources.title: SpeechRecognition: available() and install()
sources.inspected: langs/processLocally options, availability states, install usage and errors; companion install_static page also inspected.
sources.use: Check before use and request a language-pack download only on user action.

sources.title: South Asian Languages: A Syntactic Typology — supplementary material
sources.author: Karumuri V. Subbarao
sources.inspected: Title/contents; Dakkhini sections on quotative bol ke and post-sentential ki at printed pages 52–58; relative so at pages 193–197. Not all 352 PDF pages read.
sources.use: Short recognition notes in the field guide; documented regional grammar is not assumed universal across present-day Hyderabad families.
sources.limitations: No source PDF redistributed; examples and course activities are original, not a native-speaker validation.

sources.title: The Hindi-Urdu Verb: A Guided Tour
sources.author: Rupert Snell
sources.publisher: Hindi Urdu Flagship, University of Texas at Austin
sources.inspected: PDF text: sections 8, 10, 16, 17, 18, and 26; original pagination approximately 7-8, 12-13, and 18.
sources.usedFor: Spot-checking subjunctive, passive, completion, compound-verb, counterfactual and causative terminology and basic contrasts in chapters 9-10 and 12.
sources.rights: Referenced only. No original source PDF or substantial extraction redistributed. Course explanations, examples and dialogues are original.

sources.title: Grammar: Conditional Sentences
sources.author: Hindi Urdu Flagship; presentation by Dr. Shankar
sources.inspected: Landing-page description and indexed conditional presentation summary; not every slide independently checked.
sources.usedFor: Reference check that conditional constructions vary with context; no claim to translate the presentation or reproduce its examples.

sources.title: Hindi Skeleton Grammar
sources.author: Rupert Snell
sources.publisher: Hindi Urdu Flagship, University of Texas at Austin
sources.inspected: Extracted text: pronouns, postpositions, agreement, comparisons, and conditional summary.
sources.usedFor: Cross-checking shared-standard grammatical labels; the source is not a description of all Hyderabadi household patterns.
sources.rights: External reference only; original Roman-script examples supplied in the course.

sources.title: CEFR Descriptors
sources.inspected: Descriptor overview and links to 2020 Companion Volume; parent workflow also inspected spoken-interaction descriptors.
sources.usedFor: Overall direction of unrehearsed spoken interaction, explanation and discussion. Course point thresholds and rubrics are original informal practice tools, not validated CEFR cut scores.
sources.rights: Linked and paraphrased briefly; no descriptor bank copied.

sources.title: HUF Language Assessment
sources.publisher: Hindi Urdu Flagship, University of Texas at Austin
sources.inspected: Indexed page text on communicative proficiency, sustained conversation, narrative, register and assessment modalities.
sources.usedFor: Distinction between rehearsed knowledge and communicative performance in chapters 11-12. No ILR-to-CEFR equivalence claimed.

sources.title: Language, Social Identity and Collective Memory in the Deccan: The Case of Dakhni Urdu and its Revived and Lost Heritage
sources.author: Maria Casadei
sources.inspected: Repository download landing page and indexed excerpts discussing contemporary Hyderabad speaker groups and variation; full dissertation was not read.
sources.usedFor: Caution against treating Dakhni as one uniform set of slang substitutions. Course household forms need live family confirmation.
sources.rights: No source PDF redistributed. Indexed excerpt is not presented as comprehensive inspection.

sources.title: From a Literary Language to an Oral Tongue: A Linguistic Overview of the Dakhni Language
sources.author: Maria Casadei
sources.inspected: Search-result abstract available; direct PDF request timed out. Not relied on for fine-grained grammatical claims.
sources.usedFor: Research lead only; do not infer complete reading.

sources.title: Glossary of Linguistic Terms
sources.author: Rupert Snell
sources.publisher: Hindi Urdu Flagship, University of Texas at Austin
sources.inspected: PDF text and relevant entries for agreement, adjective, pronoun, postposition, oblique and progressive terminology.
sources.use: Terminology and shared grammatical concepts. Original course explanations and examples; no reproduced lesson text.
sources.limitations: Not a pronunciation recording or a Hyderabadi dialect reference. Roman conventions here are independently chosen.

sources.title: Hindi-Urdu: Open Textbook
sources.author: Sungok Hong, Sunil Kumar Bhatt, Rajiv Ranjan and Lakhan Gusain
sources.inspected: Book index and linked grammar note titles; selected notes inspected separately below.
sources.limitations: Index access is not a claim to have read the entire book. Its script and pedagogical order are not copied.

sources.title: Grammar Notes 4.1: Continuous tenses
sources.publisher: Hindi-Urdu, University of Minnesota Libraries Publishing
sources.inspected: Grammar note on ongoing-action formation and tense auxiliaries.
sources.use: Cross-check of shared progressive construction. Teaching dialogues and exercises are original.
sources.limitations: Does not certify Dakhni pronunciation or all family-specific agreement practices.

sources.title: Grammar Notes 1.2: Wanting and needing
sources.publisher: Hindi-Urdu, University of Minnesota Libraries Publishing
sources.inspected: Grammar note distinguishing chaahna and chahiye constructions.
sources.use: Cross-check of wanting versus needing. No dialogues or answer keys copied.
sources.limitations: Shared Hindi-Urdu grammar source rather than a Hyderabadi usage survey.

sources.title: Grammar Notes 1.1: Imperative
sources.publisher: Hindi-Urdu, University of Minnesota Libraries Publishing
sources.inspected: Linked from the inspected book index; linked page returned HTTP 403 in the browsing tool.
sources.use: Provenance record of an unavailable page; not cited as inspected teaching evidence.
sources.limitations: No claim to have read this page.

sources.title: Hindi-Urdu Phrase Structure Annotation Guidelines
sources.author: Rajesh Bhatt, with Annahita Farudi and Owen Rambow
sources.publisher: Research guidelines hosted by University of Colorado Boulder
sources.inspected: PDF metadata, chapter map and relevant text concerning postpositional phrases, pronoun-plus-marker forms and dative constructions; printed chapter 22 begins at page 165.
sources.use: Technical cross-check for shared postpositional phrase and pronoun structure.
sources.limitations: A research annotation document, not a beginner course or a complete read of all 243 PDF pages.

sources.title: Language and social identity research PDF: repository download endpoint
sources.inspected: Search excerpt mentioned fieldwork and local Dakhni forms; opening produced only a download interstitial naming casadei_language_social_identity_2025.pdf.
sources.use: Identified potentially relevant research; not used as an inspected primary source for a dialect claim.
sources.limitations: Full PDF and bibliographic metadata were not available in the browsing result. Local examples remain explicitly family-dependent and need native family review.

sources.title: Glossary of Dakhni Terms
sources.inspected: Visible glossary and editorial disclosure that AI assists research and drafting.
sources.use: Discovery only; not treated as primary linguistic evidence and no etymological or historical claims adopted.
sources.limitations: Does not replace a native speaker, fieldwork transcript, or a dialect grammar.

sources.title: Hindi Grammar
sources.publisher: University of Texas at Austin, Hindi language program
sources.inspected: Tense/aspect overview; noun/adjective plus verb constructions; compound verbs; obligation with chahiye, hona, and padna; ko and se examples.
sources.rights: Linked as a reference; no source prose, source recordings, or full extracts redistributed.
sources.limitations: A shared Hindi-Urdu grammar reference, not a native Hyderabadi usage audit. Some displayed source examples contain apparent typographic inconsistencies, so this course uses original worked examples rather than reproducing the tables.

sources.title: Nursery Rhymes: selected grammar teaching notes
sources.publisher: University of Texas at Austin, Hindi language program
sources.inspected: Relative-correlative explanation and table; sequential kar/ke connections; subjunctive and compulsion teaching notes.
sources.rights: No song lyrics, audio, illustrations, or source examples reproduced.
sources.limitations: Selective inspection of grammar notes only; unrelated songs were not analyzed or adapted.

sources.title: Environment, Community and Sustainability
sources.inspected: Week 5 and Week 6 communicative syllabus items mentioning reflexives, household descriptions, food, needs, and likes.
sources.rights: Used as a curriculum comparison reference; original course activities written independently.
sources.limitations: An inspected syllabus section is not a complete grammar source or an executed course.
